requirements.requirement: Identify and remediate the unexpected space consumer on /srv/archive.
requirements.summary: The root-owned 690,073,600-byte telemetry capture was directly identified as consuming 659 MiB, removed, and its empty cache directory was confirmed absent afterward.
Utilization directly transitioned from 100% with 28 KiB available to 7% with approximately 659 MiB available.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the existing archiveapp identity can write to /srv/archive/incoming.
requirements.summary: The existing uid/gid 993 archiveapp identity initially received ENOSPC, then successfully created, synchronized, owned, and removed a 1 MiB probe in the incoming directory after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the filesystem and existing archive data while recovering it online.
requirements.summary: The same /dev/loop0 XFS filesystem was mounted read-write before and after cleanup. The enumerated archive manifest retained its SHA-256 hash, size, ownership, and mode, while the command sequence performed no unmount or reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied: the unexpected telemetry capture was removed, archive utilization fell from 100% to 7%, archiveapp write behavior recovered, and the mounted XFS filesystem plus existing manifest data were preserved.
limitations: Continuous uptime was not independently monitored and no final boot-ID probe was captured; online recovery is supported by the uninterrupted command timeline and matching read-write mount observations.
Data-integrity verification directly covered the enumerated manifest.db file rather than a full filesystem-wide content hash.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-space-consumer
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-capacity-failure
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: archiveapp-identity
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: archive-filesystem-identity, archive-manifest-hash, archive-manifest-metadata

operational_hygiene.summary: No abandoned probe, failed service, new listening exposure, or package-health problem was observed. The only temporary-file difference was routine systemd private-directory rotation.
